record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the minimum number of steps of square com- pletion that are required to obtain a word from one of its factors?

evidence.quote: What is the minimum number of steps of square com- pletion that are required to obtain a word from one of its factors?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the set of finite words over $\Sigma$. A prefix-square completion step transforms a word $w \in \Sigma^*$ into $xw$ whenever $w$ has a prefix of the form $yxy$ for some $x,y \in \Sigma^*$ with $y$ nonempty (so that $yxy$ is a "square-like" factor $yxy$ where one repeats the bordering factor; equivalently, $w = yxy z$ and the step yields $xw = xyxyz$, which contains the square $(yx)^2$ as a prefix). Symmetrically, a suffix-square completion step transforms $w = z y x y$ into $wx = z y x y x$, which ends with the square $(xy)^2$. A prefix-suffix square completion step is either a prefix-square completion step or a suffix-square completion step. Write $u \Rightarrow^* v$ if $v$ can be obtained from $u$ by a finite sequence of prefix-suffix square completion steps; in this case $u$ is a factor (contiguous subword) of $v$.

Determine, as a function of $u$ and $v$ (with $u$ a factor of $v$ and $u \Rightarrow^* v$), the minimum number of prefix-suffix square completion steps needed to derive $v$ from $u$. In particular, give tight bounds, an exact formula, or an efficient algorithm computing this minimum.
artifact.status_search_result: Prefix-suffix square completion was introduced and studied by Dumitran and Manea (2015), with a linear-time decision algorithm for whether one word generates another. Follow-up work on prefix-suffix square reduction exists, but no source found explicitly resolves the minimum-number-of-steps question; status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces prefix-suffix square completion and gives a linear-time procedure deciding generation between two words.
status_evidence.claim: The framework is established but the minimum-step question is posed as a problem.

status_evidence.title: Prefix–suffix square reduction
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the inverse reduction operation; does not resolve minimum-step generation question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work does not settle the minimum-steps problem.
